content: 1. Mavorixafor: This drug can cause concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation, such as concurrent medications that increase mavorixafor exposure or other drugs with a high risk of QTc prolongation, should have their QTc interval monitored during treatment. 2. Erythromycin and Mavorixafor: Erythromycin increases mavorixafor levels or effects via inhibition of the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. If co-administered with P-gp inhibitors, reduce the mavorixafor dose as needed. 3. Erythromycin and Mefloquine: Erythromycin increases mefloquine levels or effects by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Erythromycin and Mestranol: Erythromycin increases mestranol levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition but decreases its levels by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral hormone forms and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. However, erythromycin also increases mestranol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Erythromycin and Methadone: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Erythromycin also increases methadone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Erythromycin and Methyl Aminolevulinate: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both drugs may also increase each other’s photosensitizing effects. 7. Erythromycin and Methylprednisolone: Erythromycin increases methylprednisolone levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Conversely, methylprednisolone decreases erythromycin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, but consider alternative therapy if significant interactions occur. 8. Erythromycin and Metronidazole: Metronidazole increases erythromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Erythromycin and Miconazole Vaginal: Miconazole increases erythromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 10. Erythromycin and Microbiota Oral: Erythromycin decreases the effects of oral microbiota by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Complete antibiotic regimens 2–4 days before initiating microbiota oral therapy. 11. Erythromycin and Midazolam: Erythromycin increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Co-administration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may prolong sedation due to increased systemic exposure to midazolam. 12. Erythromycin and Mifepristone: Erythromycin increases mifepristone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and mifepristone increases erythromycin levels similarly. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Erythromycin and Mipomersen: Both drugs may increase hepatic enzyme levels. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) closely. 14. Erythromycin and Mirtazapine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Erythromycin and Mitotane: Mitotane decreases erythromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely and adjust dosages as needed. 16. Erythromycin and Mitoxantrone: Erythromycin increases mitoxantrone levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Erythromycin and Mizolastine: Erythromycin increases mizolastine levels by inhibiting metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Erythromycin and Momelotinib: Erythromycin increases momelotinib toxicity via OATP1B1/B3 inhibition. Monitor closely for adverse reactions. 19. Erythromycin and Montelukast: Erythromycin increases montelukast levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Erythromycin and Moxifloxacin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Erythromycin and Nafcillin: Erythromycin decreases nafcillin effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely. 22. Erythromycin and Naldemedine: Erythromycin increases naldemedine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor for potential adverse effects. 23. Erythromycin and Naloxegol: Erythromycin increases naloxegol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Erythromycin and Nefazodone: Nefazodone increases erythromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Erythromycin and Nelfinavir: Both drugs increase each other’s levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Erythromycin and Neomycin PO: Erythromycin increases neomycin levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin and Nilotinib: Both drugs increase the QTc interval and each other’s levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Erythromycin and Nimodipine: Erythromycin increases nimodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Erythromycin and Nintedanib: Erythromycin increases nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Manage adverse effects with dose adjustments or therapy discontinuation. 30. Erythromycin and Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir: These drugs increase erythromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for increased erythromycin adverse effects, including QTc prolongation. 31. Erythromycin and Nisoldipine: Erythromycin increases nisoldipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Erythromycin and Nitrenedipine: Erythromycin increases nitrenedipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin and Norgestrel: Erythromycin increases norgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for adverse effects. 34. Erythromycin and Nortriptyline: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Erythromycin and Octreotide: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Erythromycin and Olanzapine: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Erythromycin and Olaparib: Erythromycin increases olaparib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the olaparib dose and monitor closely. 38. Erythromycin and Oliceridine: Erythromycin increases oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely for respiratory depression and sedation. 39. Erythromycin and Olodaterol: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Erythromycin and Omaveloxolone: Erythromycin increases omaveloxolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose and monitor closely. 41. Erythromycin and Ondansetron: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. ECG monitoring is recommended in high-risk patients. 42. Erythromycin and Osilodrostat: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Erythromycin and Osimertinib: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse effects. 44. Erythromycin and Oxacillin: Erythromycin decreases oxacillin effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely. 45. Erythromycin and Oxaliplatin: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Erythromycin and Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine decreases erythromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Erythromycin and Oxybutynin: Erythromycin increases oxybutynin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Erythromycin and Ozanimod: Both drugs increase the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid initiating ozanimod in patients on QT-prolonging drugs with arrhythmogenic properties. 49. Erythromycin and Paclitaxel: Erythromycin increases paclitaxel levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition and CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely.
